subject.title: OpenAI Codex OAuth can bind to a deactivated ChatGPT workspace when accounts have multiple workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw automatically recover from a deactivated ChatGPT workspace by probing/selecting/persisting another active accountId, or only surface guided relogin/remediation?
rationale: The source path proves the stale accountId can remain authoritative, but choosing automatic selection versus retry-only versus user-guided repair changes auth/profile semantics for existing users.

options.title: Define automatic recovery policy
options.body: Implement OpenAI-plugin-owned validation that can retry with Codex previous_account_id or another proven active accountId, then persist only a known-good replacement with tests and live proof.

options.title: Require guided remediation only
options.body: Keep failover classification but add Doctor/setup/UI guidance that asks the user to relogin or import the active workspace without changing stored accountId automatically.

options.title: Leave classifier mitigation as sufficient
options.body: Treat auth_permanent failover from PR #55893 as the intended behavior and close this broader workspace-selection request as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Define automatic recovery policy
recommendation.body: Implement OpenAI-plugin-owned validation that can retry with Codex previous_account_id or another proven active accountId, then persist only a known-good replacement with tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the central Codex auth ownership refactor touching the same OpenAI/Codex OAuth and bridge boundaries.
